messages:
Alex: thinking out loud — we need to finalize a default transport for internal control-plane calls (routing decisions, quota checks, rollout signals). Do we go gRPC+proto for ergonomics/typed telemetry or stick with lightweight REST+JSON for console friendliness?
Maya: +1 on typing, but worried about browser/debug UX. Console folks want easy cURL + copyable examples.
Sanjay: for high-throughput routing decisions (10k rps) gRPC gives us multiplexing and smaller wire size. Also server-streaming helps for async rollout signals.
Priya: telemetry is the real constraint — regardless of transport we need consistent attributes upstream. How do we propagate route/tenant claims + sample ids? header-based or json envelope?
Ben: header propagation is simplest: x-rd-route, x-rd-tenant, x-rd-sample. FWIW Envoy already surfaces those through LDS. Small example: 
```
GET /v1/route/evaluate
Host: infra
X-RD-Tenant: acct-123
X-RD-Route: model-route-v2
X-RD-Trace: r-abc123
```
Works with REST and gRPC gRPC-metadata.
Maya: but headers lose nested attributes (prompt-level tags). For eval sets we want a structured payload. Maybe accept both: headers for fast path, JSON body for verbose traces.
Sanjay: agree dual-mode. But then gateway needs to normalize before emitting telemetry. We should standardize a small canonical envelope we log: {tenant, route, decision_id, sampling, latency_ms}. Keep payload normalized at the gateway edge.
Priya: can we enforce that in the control plane? Little linter that fails CI if new endpoints don't emit normalized telemetry. Console team wants per-route histograms (p50/p95 per model variant) — consistent keys make dashboards composable.
Alex: rollout UX: console wants canary signals based on error budget + quality regressions. That requires structured events from inference layer — not just success/failure. Thoughts on how transport affects that?
Ben: protobufs let us version the event schema without breaking parsers. REST plus JSON also works but we need strict schema validation & a shared repo. The real ops cost is maintaining translators.
Maya: client ergonomics: if we expose a tiny SDK auto-generating proto clients for internal services, teams get typed calls. For ad-hoc debugging we still provide a REST shim (transcoding). That gives best of both.
Sanjay: beware transcoding footguns: streaming endpoints (server push) are awkward to emulate with JSON. If we rely on streaming for rollout notices, the shim must emulate via SSE or websockets. Complexity + operational surface.
Priya: quotas and rate limits: token-level vs request-level quotas. If we use gRPC with long-lived streams, quota accounting must switch to per-event or per-token framing. Implementation complexity goes up.
Alex: tradeoffs summary from this thread so far:
- gRPC+proto: better perf, typing, streaming. Harder for ad-hoc debugging, browser clients, and requires SDKs.
- REST+JSON: universal, simple for console & cURL, worse at streaming and wire efficiency.
- Hybrid: proto-first with REST transcoding shim at gateway. Normalize telemetry at gateway. Enforce schemas via CI lint.
Maya: +hybrid. Add: document quick troubleshooting steps: how to curl the shim, how to run proto client, where telemetry keys live.
Ben: operational checklist: logging contract, quota accounting doc, transcoder limitations, canary signal shapes. I can draft a PR.
Priya: also add migration guidance: how to version fields (v1 -> v2) and deprecation window. Include console screenshot mocks for signal UX.
Sanjay: curious: anyone measured p99 latency delta between REST and gRPC on our infra? If not, let's A/B a small endpoint -> add datapoint to the PR.
Alex: good call. @deploy-bot can we spin an experiment on route-eval (10% traffic) for 24h comparing grpc vs rest shim latency & tail?
deploy-bot: scheduled experiment 'transport-interop-eval' for route-eval: start=1765010000, duration=86400s, cohorts=[grpc,rest-shim], notify=#eng-platform on completion :rocket:
Maya: sweet. while that's running I'll start a docs PR describing header keys + canonical envelope. Ben, Priya — collab on telemetry contract?
Ben: on it.
Priya: will add dashboard wireframes.
Alex: thanks all — we'll reconvene after the experiment. Short action items in thread: draft PR (Ben), telemetry contract (Priya + Ben), docs + troubleshooting (Maya), experiment scheduled (deploy-bot).
